title: Configure orchestrator providers and models in Settings with runtime discovery
body:
Add Settings UI for controlling which providers and exact models the orchestrator may use on this installation. The user must be able to enable or disable Grok, Claude, Codex, or individual models as availability and quality change, without editing bundled skills or changing their manual CLI defaults.

Recommended design to refine:
- Persist an installation-local orchestration policy: enabled providers, allowed model IDs, preferred choices for routine work and difficult reasoning/research, and permitted fallbacks. No fixed Claude/Codex default. Separate user choices from detected capabilities.
- Show installed CLI/version, supported model selection, and model access as verified available, unavailable, or unknown, with source and last-checked time. Installation, authentication, account entitlement, quota, and model quality are distinct facts; do not infer access or current quota from an installed executable.
- Prefer supported CLI/provider discovery. Preserve a manual model entry/override when discovery is incomplete; unknown must not be displayed as unavailable. Discovery should not launch paid inference or scrape private credentials/config formats. An API model list does not automatically prove access through the CLI account.
- Provide an explicit refresh. Catalog updates can suggest newly discovered models but must preserve disabled providers, exact selections, and user preferences; never silently enable Grok or switch models after an update. Cache results and handle offline/stale information.
- Expose the effective policy and runtime capabilities through the Foreman control CLI so cold orchestrators consult them before dispatch. Bundled skills describe selection principles and query that policy instead of owning a static operational allowlist. Enforce orchestration exclusions at dispatch, including fallbacks; make the boundary with manual sessions explicit.
- Report why a model was chosen and why no eligible model can run. Never silently downgrade an explicitly requested model or substitute a disabled provider. Respect the policy at subsequent dispatches without interrupting existing workers.
- Investigate supported Grok model-selection flags and account-aware discovery before adding explicit Grok model overrides; v0.8.3 supports --model only for Claude/Codex. Keep model access separate from dated cost/quality recommendations; capability discovery cannot determine which model is best.

Acceptance examples: disabling Grok prevents automatic selection even when installed; enabling it makes only eligible configured models candidates; missing/unknown/offline states are honest; refresh and app upgrades preserve preferences; a cold orchestrator sees the same effective policy as Settings; dispatch rejects excluded models and does not bypass exclusions via a fallback.

Start from src/settings.rs, src/config.rs, src/agent_command.rs, src/control.rs, src/wm.rs, docs/kanban-board.md, and both foreman-kanban/orchestrating-plans.md copies. Read the architecture and config/flags reference skills before implementation. Add persistence/defaulting, eligibility/fallback, and control-plane compatibility tests; verify GUI changes with screenshot evidence; update existing subsystem docs and both bundled skill copies. Build safely inside Foreman with --target-dir target/agent.
